description.value: The study investigated neuroanatomic correlates of the ability to use paralinguistic cues to recognize sarcasm in patients with neurodegenerative disease using structural MRI and voxel-based morphometry.

spans.text: We investigated the neuroanatomic correlates of the ability to use paralinguistic cues to recognize sarcasm in patients with neurodegenerative disease by first testing subjects with a psychometrically validated measure of sarcasm comprehension, then performing quantitative analysis of structural MRI scans.

description.value: Ninety subjects, including patients with six neurodegenerative diseases and healthy older controls, underwent behavioral assessment and structural MRI.

spans.text: Patients were recruited into the study from a dementia specialty clinic.

description.value: Subjects watched brief videos depicting sincere or sarcastic communication and answered yes–no questions about the speaker's intended meaning.

spans.text: Subjects watched brief videos depicting sincere or sarcastic communication and answered yes–no questions about the speaker's intended meaning.
Sincere (SIN)
In the Sincere condition, the speaker's non-verbal cues are consistent with the verbal content

description.value: Five intermixed video vignettes in which neutral scripted verbal content and the speaker's facial, vocal, and bodily cues were consistent, so the manifest verbal content accurately conveyed the speaker's sincere intended meaning; participants answered four yes–no questions per item.

spans.text: In the Sincere condition, the speaker's non-verbal cues are consistent with the verbal content, thus no irony is implied, and the verbal content accurately signifies the speaker's intended meaning.
Simple Sarcasm (SSR)
In the Simple Sarcasm condition, the speaker uses exaggerated facial, vocal, and body language indicating sarcasm

description.value: Five intermixed video vignettes in which neutral scripted verbal content was paired with exaggerated facial, vocal, and bodily cues indicating sarcasm; the speaker's intended ironic meaning diverged from the manifest verbal content, and participants answered four yes–no questions per item.

spans.text: In the Simple Sarcasm condition, the speaker uses exaggerated facial, vocal, and body language indicating sarcasm, thus their intended meaning is ironic and diverges from the manifest verbal content of their speech.
Subjects watch 10 brief (less than 1 min) video vignettes in which professional actors interact

instructions.value: Participants watched brief video vignettes and answered four yes–no questions about the characters' actions, thoughts, words, and emotions, identifying the speaker's intended meaning.

spans.text: Subjects watch 10 brief (less than 1 min) video vignettes in which professional actors interact, and then answer four yes–no questions about the actions, thoughts, words, and emotions of the characters.

stimuli.value: Ten brief, less-than-one-minute video vignettes of professional actors interacting: five sincere and five simple-sarcasm items, intermixed after an unscored practice video. Verbal content was neutral; paralinguistic cues included facial expression, voice prosody, hand and head gestures, and body posture.
